name: constraint_reasoning

messages.content: Think carefully and answer with the minimal reasoning needed to justify the result.

A job can run on GPU A or GPU B. GPU A is 30% faster but can only run one job at a time. GPU B can run two jobs at a time but each job takes 80 minutes. There are three identical jobs. What schedule minimizes total elapsed time, and why?

quality_rubric: A high-quality answer recognizes that GPU B can run two jobs in parallel, GPU A should run the third concurrently, and the makespan is bounded by the two B jobs at 80 minutes. It should explain why putting more jobs on A does not beat 80 minutes. Accept either common interpretation of '30% faster' for A's exact single-job duration if the optimal schedule and 80-minute makespan are correct.
must_include: two jobs on GPU B concurrently
one job on GPU A concurrently

name: architecture_tradeoff

messages.content: You evaluate engineering tradeoffs with concrete operational implications.

Compare a single llama.cpp router process with one loaded model at a time against one long-running server per model. Focus on latency, memory pressure, operational complexity, and benchmarking consistency.

quality_rubric: A high-quality answer compares cold-load versus warm latency, resident RAM/GPU memory pressure, operational complexity, routing/control-plane simplicity, failure isolation, and benchmarking consistency. It should explicitly connect one-loaded-model routing to memory conservation and per-model servers to faster warm switching at higher memory cost.
